catalog_quote: Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable. ... [p. 96, language notes:] Selayar. In some words Selayar diverges from the usual South Sulawesi penultimate syllable stress pattern and exhibits antepenultimate stress. ... Mamuju. The Padang and Sinyonyoi dialects use [h] where the other dialects use [w] and /r/. Tappalang and Botteng substitute [h] for [w], but not for /r/. Mamuju and Sumare retain both [w] and /r/.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (216 pdf pp., Pacific Linguistics D-78 scan). Printed p. 94 (pdf p. 102), Appendix E 'Comparative word lists', SYMBOLS block, reads exactly: "Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable." (extracted text shows only scanned letter-spacing differences.) Surrounding section: p. 96 language notes flag only Selayar for antepenultimate deviations; the Mamuju note says Tappalang and Botteng substitute [h] for [w] and says nothing on stress.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress on the penultimate syllable as the South Sulawesi norm; the compilers' Tappalang and Botteng wordlists (the two lects now classified as Ulumanda') are left unmarked for stress, i.e. treated as regular penultimate, with no Ulumanda'-specific deviation noted (only Selayar is flagged for antepenultimate deviations).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Tappalang/Botteng. Generic caveat that stress may be unclear with double vocoids (long vowels); the one apostrophe in the Botteng rows (' dodo i) is a doubtful scanned token in a 216-page scan and was not verified against the image.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-level generalisation over 38 South Sulawesi wordlists (c. 200 citation-form lexical items each, elicited in isolation); not a description of Ulumanda'. Grimes & Grimes filed Tappalang and Botteng as dialects of MAMUJU (pp. 36-39, fn. 9 p. 204); their reassignment to Ulumanda' comes from Strømme & Valkama 1987:87 and Friberg & Laskowske 1989:6-8. Sister-language PUS/Bambam (Campbell 1991:10-11) is explicitly penultimate with suffix-driven rightward shift and final vocative stress, consistent with the group pattern but not evidence for Ulumanda'.
new_statements.identity_note: No description of Ulumanda' as such exists. The only stress statement covering Ulumanda' data is the group-level remark in Grimes & Grimes 1987, whose Tappalang and Botteng wordlists (nos. 16-17) they classified as dialects of Mamuju [mqx, mamu1255]; Strømme & Valkama 1987 and Friberg & Laskowske 1989 reassigned Botteng-Tappalang (plus Awo' Sumakuyu and Sondoang) to Ulumanda' [ulm, ulum1237], which is how Glottolog/Ethnologue list them today (Botteng-Tappalang is a Glottolog alternative name for ulum1237). The earlier scan's 'Smith 1993' is a Proto-PUS reconstruction with Ulumanda' (Botteng, Kiha', Kondo etc.) wordlists, not a descriptive phonology; Campbell 1991 'Phonology of Pitu Ulunna Salu' (held by the project) describes the sister language Bambam [ptu, bamb1270], Salumokanam dialect, not Ulumanda'.

sources.citation: Zobel, Erik. 2014 (15 Sep). Vowel Fronting in Ulumanda' (South Sulawesi). Blog post, Sounds from around the Pacific Ocean (ezlinguistics.blogspot.com).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only first-hand phonological material on Ulumanda' found: 8-vowel system (a/ä, o/ö, u/ü + e, i) with contrast only in final closed root syllables and regressive vowel harmony; Kabira'an-dialect informant plus Smith 1993 Kiha' data. 'Accent' occurs once, in the sense of a foreign-sounding accent in Indonesian.
